stem: Which intervention is appropriate for maintaining an indwelling urinary catheter drainage system and reducing CAUTI risk?

options.A: Disconnect the catheter and tubing once per shift to rinse the tubing and inspect the connection.
options.B: Keep the drainage bag below bladder level by resting it on the floor beside the bed.
options.C: Maintain a closed drainage system, keep the catheter and tubing free of kinks, and keep the bag below bladder level and off the floor.
options.D: Replace the catheter and collection bag every day even when the closed system remains intact and no clinical indication exists.

rationale: CDC CAUTI prevention recommendations direct healthcare personnel to maintain a closed drainage system after aseptic catheter insertion, maintain unobstructed urine flow, keep the catheter and collecting tube free from kinking, and keep the collecting bag below bladder level without resting it on the floor. CDC also advises against routine fixed-interval catheter or drainage-bag changes; changes should be based on clinical indications or compromise of the closed system. Therefore C is correct. A disrupts the closed system, B places the bag on the floor, and D uses an unnecessary fixed replacement schedule.
educational_objective: Reduce CAUTI risk by maintaining a closed, unobstructed urinary drainage system with kink-free tubing and a collection bag kept below bladder level and off the floor.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Guideline for Prevention of Catheter-Associated Urinary Tract Infections — Summary of Recommendations
source_version_date: CDC web summary March 25, 2024; guideline currentness live-rechecked August 16, 2026
source_locator: III.A: maintain a closed drainage system. III.B-III.B.2: maintain unobstructed urine flow, keep catheter/collecting tube free from kinking, keep bag below bladder at all times and do not rest it on floor. III.E: routine fixed-interval catheter/drainage-bag changes are not recommended; change for clinical indications or closed-system compromise.
source_claim_supported: CAUTI prevention includes a closed drainage system, unobstructed kink-free flow, the bag below bladder level and off the floor, and avoidance of unnecessary fixed-interval system changes.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: apply infection-prevention practices, maintain invasive devices safely, and reduce healthcare-associated infection risk.
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — indwelling urinary catheter maintenance and CAUTI prevention

source_original.stem: Which intervention is most important for maintaining an indwelling urinary catheter drainage system and reducing CAUTI risk?

options.A: Disconnect the catheter and tubing once per shift to rinse the tubing and inspect the connection.
options.B: Keep the drainage bag below bladder level by resting it on the floor beside the bed.
options.C: Maintain a closed system, keep tubing free of kinks, and keep the bag below the bladder and off the floor.
options.D: Replace the catheter and collection bag every day even when the closed system remains intact.

source_original.rationale: CDC recommends a closed drainage system with unobstructed flow, kink-free tubing, and a collection bag kept below bladder level without touching the floor. Option C is correct. Routine disconnection, floor placement, and fixed daily replacement increase risk or contradict guideline recommendations.
source_original.source_detail: Maintenance recommendations: maintain a closed drainage system and unobstructed urine flow; keep catheter/tubing free of kinks; keep the collection bag below bladder level and off the floor; do not change catheters/bags at routine fixed intervals. Current CDC CAUTI recommendations live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: transmission precautions, PPE, device/environmental safety, asepsis, identification and infection-prevention activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the CAUTI maintenance construct and key C. Removed the vague 'most important' hierarchy from the stem because the CDC recommendations are complementary maintenance practices, and tightened D to preserve the guideline's clinical-indication exception to fixed-interval replacement.

audit_findings.clinical_category: CAUTI prevention and urinary drainage-system maintenance
audit_findings.source_authority: Current CDC CAUTI prevention guidance; official NCSBN 2026 blueprint
audit_findings.currentness: CDC CAUTI web guideline current in 2026 and live-rechecked 2026-08-16
audit_findings.exact_locator: CDC Summary of Recommendations III.A, III.B-III.B.2, and III.E
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item uses only explicit CDC device-maintenance recommendations and preserves the clinical-indication exception for catheter/bag changes.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect because unnecessary disconnection compromises the closed drainage system.
distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because the bag must not rest on the floor.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because routine fixed-interval replacement is not recommended when no clinical indication or system compromise exists.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only C combines all required maintenance principles without violating another CDC recommendation.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are urinary drainage-system maintenance actions and are parallel in scope.
audit_findings.blueprint: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — invasive-device and healthcare-associated infection prevention.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked current CDC recommendations, all four options, rationale, objective, NCSBN mapping, ambiguity and cueing. C remained uniquely correct.
